response:
Final-round reflection: the archive now supports a clear production function, and the closing batch should exploit it while settling the last structural question. **Alpha** is driven by the persistence value leg (TS_MIN of the pre-research earnings yield: α 8.0%, t 5.75) and by funding/solvency conditioners (cliff α 7.4%, cash × R&D α 6.9%, debt coverage α 5.6%). **Cross-sectional slope** is driven by peer-relative products (fmb 6.7–6.9), the suppression share (6.40), and the weakest-link rule (6.39). **Sharpe** is driven by hard-book and coverage screens (0.50–0.53). The persistence leg's weakness is exactly what the reliability screens fix (its Sharpe is only 0.34), and the reliability screens' weakness — modest alpha — is exactly what persistence fixes, so pairing them across *non-overlapping variables* (the critic's entanglement point) is the highest-prior consolidation available. Two failures also still deserve repair: the industry-mean soft-book conditioner degenerated into a sector tilt (α 1.4%), and the liquid+knowledge anchor has real alpha (5.6%) but almost no slope (fmb 1.73), which suggests it needs a flow-based partner rather than a screen.

---SIGNAL 1---
NAME: Neglected Solvent Self-Builder
EXPRESSION: SUMRANK(TS_MIN(RATIO(ADD(ib, COALESCE(xrd, 0)), MUL(prcc_f, csho)), 5), SUMRANK(WINSOR(SUB(RATIO(TS_SUM(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 5), at), RATIO(COALESCE(intan, 0), at)), 1), WINSOR(RATIO(ADD(ebitda, COALESCE(xrd, 0)), ADD(dltt, dlc)), 1)))
HYPOTHESIS: The complete intangible-value case requires three independent facts: the discount has persisted for five years (durable neglect), the firm's intangible capital is self-built rather than purchased (the book genuinely understates capital), and pre-research cash flow covers total debt many times over (the program cannot be forced to stop).
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: These are the three highest-performing components discovered in the run that share no variable across legs — the composition term uses only stocks scaled by assets and the coverage term uses only flows scaled by debt, so neither can mechanically inflate the persistence numerator, which was the critic's objection to the earlier splice. Each channel repairs a specific weakness of the others: persistence supplies alpha (8.0%), composition supplies Sharpe (0.45), and debt coverage supplies the cross-sectional slope (5.62).
INTERACTION_TYPE: composite

---SIGNAL 2---
NAME: Conjunctive Neglect Composition and Solvency
EXPRESSION: MIN(RANK(TS_MIN(RATIO(ADD(ib, COALESCE(xrd, 0)), MUL(prcc_f, csho)), 5)), MIN(RANK(WINSOR(SUB(RATIO(TS_SUM(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 5), at), RATIO(COALESCE(intan, 0), at)), 1)), RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(ADD(ebitda, COALESCE(xrd, 0)), ADD(dltt, dlc)), 1))))
HYPOTHESIS: Persistence, composition and solvency are non-substitutable: a five-year discount is worthless if the balance sheet is an acquisition roll-up, and clean self-built capital is worthless if creditors will force the research program to be cut, so the binding constraint should price the security rather than the average of the three.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: The conjunctive rule has beaten compensatory averaging on cross-sectional slope every time it has been tested (weakest-link fmb 6.39, binding-constraint fmb 5.20 with α 6.4%), and this applies it to the identical inputs used additively in Signal 1, so the pair delivers the run's cleanest verdict on aggregation form with all channels held fixed. The MIN operator also caps the influence of any single extreme rank, which is where the multiplicative peer signals lost Sharpe.
INTERACTION_TYPE: novel

---SIGNAL 3---
NAME: Persistent Discount on a Hard Balance Sheet
EXPRESSION: SUMRANK(TS_MIN(RATIO(ADD(ib, COALESCE(xrd, 0)), MUL(prcc_f, csho)), 5), SUMRANK(NEG(RATIO(COALESCE(gdwl, 0), at)), NEG(RATIO(ADD(dltt, dlc), SUB(at, COALESCE(intan, 0))))))
HYPOTHESIS: A discount that has lasted five years is trustworthy precisely when the book against which it is measured is hard — unpadded by goodwill and with debt covered by pledgeable tangible assets — so durable neglect plus balance-sheet integrity should isolate mismeasured firms from slowly failing ones.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: The hard-book conditioner pair produced the archive's best Sharpe (0.534) with α 6.2% but used a single-year value leg, while the persistence leg produced the best alpha with the worst Sharpe of the leaders (0.34); combining them addresses each one's documented deficiency and neither conditioner shares a variable with the persistence numerator. This is the natural closing test of whether the alpha from durable neglect survives a strict accounting-integrity screen.
INTERACTION_TYPE: composite

---SIGNAL 4---
NAME: Dual Anchor Intangible Value
EXPRESSION: SUMRANK(RATIO(ADD(ib, COALESCE(xrd, 0)), MUL(prcc_f, csho)), RATIO(ADD(che, TS_SUM(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 5)), MUL(prcc_f, csho)))
HYPOTHESIS: A firm is unambiguously cheap only when both views of it agree: the going-concern view, that its pre-research earnings are large relative to price, and the realizable view, that its cash plus accumulated knowledge capital is large relative to price; firms cheap on only one anchor are either earnings-cyclical or asset-rich shells.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: This repairs the diagnosed weakness of the liquid-and-knowledge anchor, which delivered α 5.6% (t 5.02) but a near-null slope of 1.73 because a stock-based anchor orders the cross-section poorly on its own; pairing it with the flow yield, whose slope is reliably 4–5, should restore cross-sectional information without sacrificing the anchor's alpha. It is deliberately parsimonious — two valuation views, no quality screen — so the result isolates whether anchor disagreement is the operative source of noise.
INTERACTION_TYPE: composite

---SIGNAL 5---
NAME: Accounting Loss Economic Profit
EXPRESSION: SUMRANK(RATIO(ADD(ib, COALESCE(xrd, 0)), MUL(prcc_f, csho)), SUB(INDICATOR(ADD(ib, COALESCE(xrd, 0)), 0), INDICATOR(ib, 0)))
HYPOTHESIS: The sharpest possible statement of the research brief's premise is the set of firms that report a loss but are profitable before research spending; these firms are mechanically excluded by earnings screens, profitability factors and many institutional mandates even though their economic income is positive, so they should carry an abnormal return that plain earnings yield cannot capture.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: Every archive signal treats the R&D add-back as continuous, but the mispricing it describes is most acute at a discrete boundary — the sign flip of reported income — and no signal has isolated the group where the add-back actually changes a firm's classification from loss-making to profitable. The conditioner equals one only for that group and zero for everyone else, giving a clean, interpretable tilt whose result directly tests whether the expensing distortion is priced at the classification margin rather than smoothly.
INTERACTION_TYPE: novel

---SIGNAL 6---
NAME: Peer Neglected Innovator
EXPRESSION: MUL(IND_RANK(WINSOR(TS_MIN(RATIO(ADD(ib, COALESCE(xrd, 0)), MUL(prcc_f, csho)), 5), 1)), IND_RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(TS_SUM(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 5), at), 1)))
HYPOTHESIS: The most mispriced firm in an industry is the one that has been persistently cheaper than its direct competitors for five consecutive years while carrying the largest accumulated research stock relative to assets — sustained peer-relative neglect of the industry's biggest knowledge investor.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: The peer-relative conjunctive product family owns the archive's highest cross-sectional slopes (6.88, 6.93, 6.73) but consistently middling alpha, while the persistence leg owns the highest alpha with a weak slope, so replacing the single-year yield inside the peer product with the five-year minimum targets exactly the metric each family lacks. Industry ranking both legs also removes the sector concentration that plagues raw research-intensity sorts, and coverage stays near 0.14.
INTERACTION_TYPE: conditional

---CRITIQUE Neglected Solvent Self-Builder---
VERDICT: accept
SCORE: 3
RATIONALE: Internally consistent and the three legs are genuinely non-overlapping in variables, but it is essentially a mechanical three-way splice of the archive's top-performing components chosen on realized metrics, so it carries obvious selection/overfitting risk and offers limited new economic content.

---CRITIQUE Conjunctive Neglect Composition and Solvency---
VERDICT: flag
SCORE: 3
RATIONALE: The conjunctive-aggregation question was already answered twice in the archive (weakest-link and binding-constraint signals), and two of the three legs here are conceptually the same as the gen-8 MIN composite (persistence, funding adequacy), so the marginal evidence is a leg substitution rather than a new test.

---CRITIQUE Persistent Discount on a Hard Balance Sheet---
VERDICT: flag
SCORE: 2
RATIONALE: This is the archived Hard-Book Value Composite with the value leg swapped for its five-year minimum — a cosmetic variant of two already-tested signals whose likely outcome is a blend of their known metrics.

---CRITIQUE Dual Anchor Intangible Value---
VERDICT: flag
SCORE: 3
RATIONALE: Both legs share the same market-cap denominator, so the "two independent views" framing overstates the construct — the composite is largely a double-weighted 1/P (value/size) tilt built from two already-tested anchors, i.e., a standard composite-value rediscovery rather than a new mechanism.

---CRITIQUE Accounting Loss Economic Profit---
VERDICT: accept
SCORE: 4
RATIONALE: The conditioner correctly and cleanly isolates the discrete set of firms that flip from reported loss to pre-R&D profit (it can only take values 0 or 1 given xrd ≥ 0), which is a genuinely untested classification-margin hypothesis, though the binary rank creates a large tie mass so the tilt will be modest and the group overlaps with known loss/distress effects that could push against the expected sign.

---CRITIQUE Peer Neglected Innovator---
VERDICT: flag
SCORE: 2
RATIONALE: This sits directly at the intersection of two archived signals (Peer-Relative Cheap Innovator and Persistently Cheap Innovator), differing only by substituting TS_MIN for the current-year yield inside an existing IND_RANK product, which is the kind of cosmetic variant the objective warns against.

---SIGNAL 1---
NAME: Worst-Case Research Debt Coverage
EXPRESSION: SUMRANK(RATIO(ADD(ib, COALESCE(xrd, 0)), MUL(prcc_f, csho)), WINSOR(TS_MIN(RATIO(ADD(ebitda, COALESCE(xrd, 0)), ADD(dltt, dlc)), 5), 1))
HYPOTHESIS: What protects an unpledgeable research program is not this year's debt coverage but the coverage the firm sustained in its worst year of the cycle; a cheap innovator whose pre-research cash flow covered its debt even at the trough never faced a creditor-forced program cut, while one that dipped to thin coverage once has already demonstrated it can be squeezed.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
INTERACTION_TYPE: composite
REASONING: The downside-state transformation is the single most reliably productive design choice in this archive — it turned failing symmetric conditioners into winners three separate times (margin floor α 5.4%, pre-research earnings floor α 5.4%, demand floor α 7.1%) — and it has never been applied to the flow-solvency channel discovered only last generation (fmb 5.62, Sharpe 0.50). Unlike a leg substitution inside an existing aggregation, this changes what the conditioner measures: chronic debt-service capacity rather than a single-year snapshot that debt issuance or a good year can flatter.

---SIGNAL 2---
NAME: Innovation Efficiency Gap
EXPRESSION: SUMRANK(RATIO(ADD(ib, COALESCE(xrd, 0)), MUL(prcc_f, csho)), SUB(IND_RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), revt), 1)), IND_RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(MA(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 3), at), 1))))
HYPOTHESIS: Research spending is an input and pricing power is the output, so the informative quantity is the gap between them: a firm earning peer-beating margins on below-peer research spending has efficient, durable know-how, while a firm out-spending peers without out-earning them is burning cash on undifferentiated development that its expensed accounting hides as investment.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
INTERACTION_TYPE: composite
REASONING: The archive has only ever tested research effort and realized differentiation as complements (the gen-6 product form required both to be high, fmb 6.23), never as an input-output ratio where spending enters negatively conditional on margins — a genuinely falsifiable and opposite-signed claim about the same two variables. The signed rank difference is bounded, industry-neutral on both legs, and full coverage, and it directly addresses the run's unresolved question of whether intangible *intensity* or intangible *productivity* is the priced attribute.

---SIGNAL 3---
NAME: Liquid Knowledge Capital Share
EXPRESSION: SUMRANK(RATIO(ADD(ib, COALESCE(xrd, 0)), MUL(prcc_f, csho)), WINSOR(RATIO(ADD(che, TS_SUM(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 5)), ADD(at, TS_SUM(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 5))), 1))
HYPOTHESIS: The larger the fraction of a firm's true economic capital that consists of cash and accumulated knowledge rather than operating assets, the wider the gap between what the balance sheet shows and what the firm actually owns, so cheapness in such firms is most likely to be measurement error rather than a fair discount for asset risk.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
INTERACTION_TYPE: composite
REASONING: This replaces the double-1/P construction the critic identified with a strictly price-free conditioner: the second leg now shares no denominator with the value leg and instead measures the *composition* of the intangible-inclusive capital base, which the archive has probed one component at a time (cash-to-assets, R&D-to-assets, intangibles-to-assets) but never as the combined share of capital that accounting either omits or holds at face value. The ratio is bounded in [0,1] with a strictly positive denominator, so it cannot produce the winsorization artifacts that killed earlier asset-composition attempts.

---SIGNAL 4---
NAME: Dividend-Certified Research Intensity
EXPRESSION: SUMRANK(RATIO(ADD(ib, COALESCE(xrd, 0)), MUL(prcc_f, csho)), MUL(INDICATOR(MA(COALESCE(dvc, 0), 3), 0), RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(MA(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 3), at), 1))))
HYPOTHESIS: A research-intensity tilt is only safe when the research is demonstrably funded from real cash flow, and a sustained dividend is the hardest available certification of that: among payers, higher R&D intensity marks hidden capital, while among non-payers the same intensity may simply mark cash burn that will end in dilution.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
INTERACTION_TYPE: conditional
REASONING: This is a certification switch rather than a valuation leg — unlike the gen-2 dividend signal, which used dividend yield as the price anchor and earned α 4.0% — and it resolves a specific inconsistency in the archive, where raw R&D intensity helped in some conditioners and reversed in others depending on which firms populated the extreme deciles. The three-year averaged payout indicator turns the intensity tilt off entirely for non-payers, so the long leg contains only innovators whose programs coexist with a distributed cash surplus.
